title: Spark briefing: customer threads and priority suture
content:
Executive summary:

Quick take: this note bundles 18 recent customer threads (last 8 weeks) into 6 actionable asks + 4 low-effort mitigations. Patterns: (1) intermittent latency spikes on cold starts affecting chat sessions, (2) confusion about routing fallbacks when dedicated capacity is exhausted, (3) embedding consistency regressions for multi-tenant telemetry, (4) desire for per-route token cost visibility at the SDK level.

Why this matters: these threads are driving churn risk for 3 large mid-market accounts and 7 startups doing real-time assistants. Fixes are a mix of product UX patches, runtime fallbacks, and short eval guardrails that map to low-to-medium engineering effort but high customer confidence wins.

Contents of this doc: annotated vignettes, prioritized feature asks with hypothesis/impact/effort, quick mitigations (<= 2 engineer-days), open questions & recommended owners, next three steps.

Annotated vignettes (short raw captures):

1) Retail assistant startup (thread 1): observed 400–800ms cold-start spikes when using embedding-heavy retrieval + chat; customer instrumented prefix caching but still sees variability after model switch. Quote: "We lose context mid-flow if a request hits the wrong routing tier." Links: Slack thread + trace screenshots in linked artifacts.

2) Healthcare ISV (thread 5): worried about Dedicated -> Hosted fallback during maintenance windows. They want explicit visibility + deterministic policy (no silent fallback). Risk: compliance/QA teams flagging unexpected model variants.

3) Search/knowledge graph vendor (thread 8): embeddings drift between model v1.3 and v1.4 (quantized variant). They want a simple diff test harness or a per-deployment embedding regression alert.

4) Fintech customer (thread 12): token-level charges are opaque when SDK-level batching/caching occurs. Their billing reconciliation team cannot match session-level events to invoices.

Prioritized feature asks (sorted by customer impact & internal ROI):

A) Route-fallback transparency + opt-in strict-fallback mode
- Hypothesis: Giving enterprises an explicit policy and observable event when fallback happens reduces incidents escalations by ~60% for those customers.
- What to build: API flag (fallback_policy = [strict|allow_compatible]) + server-side event log and UI marker in console per request.
- Impact: Medium effort, high trust increase; narrows compliance risk.
- Suggested owner: product-hosted-api + SRE.

B) Embedding regression smoke-tests for model rollouts
- Hypothesis: Lightweight diff checks (cosine similarity on canonical probe set) prevent silent quality regressions on quantized/variant models.
- What to build: small harness that runs n=100 canonical vectors, stores baseline signatures, and fails rollout if average drift > threshold. Hook into rollout pipeline.
- Impact: Low-to-medium effort, prevents multiple VOC asks.
- Suggested owner: applied-ml + release-engineering.

C) SDK token-visibility export for batched/cached requests
- Hypothesis: If SDK emits a reconciliation file (session_id -> tokens_sent -> tokens_billed_estimate), finance teams can reconcile quickly and reduce billing tickets.
- What to build: SDK-level option to log batching boundaries and cache-hits, plus a console importer to map to invoices.
- Impact: Medium effort across SDK & console; immediate operational win.

D) Cold-start latency mitigation checklist + telemetry tilt
- Hypothesis: Customers can reduce user-facing cold-start spikes by following a deterministic checklist (warm-up calls, pinned KV prefixes) and seeing a cold-start metric.
- What to build: docs + an onboarding micro-runbook + a telemetry tag that surfaces % of requests that saw cold-start > 200ms in console.
- Impact: Low effort (docs + minor telemetry) but high UX payoff.

E) Per-route cost breakdown in UI (token-level and amortized model cost)
- Hypothesis: Product teams want to see cost per route to decide on model pinning/quantization tradeoffs.
- What to build: console report showing tokens, model unit cost, cache-savings estimate per route.
- Impact: Medium engineering effort on console/analytics stack; high product value.

F) Quick: show fallback-sourced request marker in API responses
- Hypothesis: Exposing a small header/field when a response was served by a fallback variant reduces troubleshooting time.
- What to build: X-Fallback-Variant header + mapping to console trace.
- Impact: Minimal runtime change; high operational ROI.

Quick mitigations (<= 2 engineer-days or docs):

- Patch: document recommended fallback policy for enterprise customers and add FAQ to PS handoff (owner: customer-success; est. 1 day).
- Patch: enable small debug header for affected customers (owner: serving-runtime; est. 1–2 days).
- Patch: distribute a "warm-start" snippet for SDKs with best practices (owner: developer-experience; est. 1 day).
- Patch: provide a one-pager on embedding drift explanation + mitigation steps for CS to send to customers (owner: applied-ml + customer-success; est. 1 day).

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):

- What is current sensitivity of the rollout pipeline to embedding drift? Need to confirm thresholds and existing telemetry (ask release-engineering & applied-ml).
- How intrusive is a strict-fallback mode on capacity (i.e., do we reject traffic or queue)? Needs SRE cost modeling.
- Can we emit an SDK reconciliation file without exposing PII/PHI for regulated customers? (Privacy check with security/compliance).

Customer quotes to cite in outreach:

- "When our assistant blanks mid-session the user abandons flow — it costs us real revenue." (Retail startup lead)
- "We need to know if a model downgrade happened during our maintenance window — we can't have surprises." (Healthcare product owner)

Recommended short timeline (next 6 weeks):

Week 0–1: ship the debug header for fallback marker (serving-runtime, 1 sprint), create FAQ + warm-start snippet (dx + cs).
Week 2–3: prioritize embedding smoke-test PoC in release pipeline (applied-ml + release-eng).
Week 3–5: design console per-route cost mockups and gather billing stake-holders (product + finance).
Week 4–6: implement SDK reconciliation export spec (dx + infra) and run pilot with 2 customers.

Who to loop in now:

- Noah Kim (SRE) — feasibility on strict-fallback model and capacity implications.
- Jules Moreno (applied-ml) — sketch for embedding smoke-test and canonical probe set.
- Rina Desai (product-hosted-api) — console mockups for per-route cost and fallback visibility.
- Release-eng lead — hook for rollout pipeline gating.

Action items (owner / due):

- Asha: compile canonical probe candidates and share by 2029-06-07.
- Noah: run quick capacity model for strict-fallback and share 2029-06-10.
- Jules: mock PoC for embedding diff tool by 2029-06-14.
- Rina: console mockup slides by 2029-06-18.

Appendix: raw signal index (internal references)

- Threads included: #4521, #4535, #4598, #4602, #4620, #4643 (internal tracker IDs).
- Example traces: stored in GH-789/replay-traces.
- Customer contacts: retail-startup@example.com (PM: Colin Y), healthcare-ISV@example.com (PD: Mira K), fintech-corp@example.com (Eng: O. Singh).

Notes to self / conversational scraps:

- Consider an "opt-in strict mode" with a soft-fallback policy: for the first N minutes after a planned maintenance window, keep strict and then auto-fall back (gives customers a short window to validate).
- Could we reuse existing KV-caching telemetry to estimate cold-start probability per route? If yes, low-cost metric addition.

End-of-file: quick send to stakeholders after review.

-- Asha
